title: Image-align more physical line transitions and calibrate predecessor comparisons across endpoint class frequencies
statement: A scan-first audit found separate consecutive baselines for all 50 selected transition pairs on 10 public practice folios. The outgoing and incoming word positions were mapped in 44 pairs; six have uncertain edge grouping. Requiring all of the compared words to pass the uncertainty filter in ZL, IT and RF left 26 matched triplets on eight folios. With pooled within-line association transferred to event-specific baselines, first-to-second minus cross-line gain is +0.0156, +0.0177 and +0.0138 nats per target in ZL, IT and RF. Midpoint minus cross-line gain is −0.0240, +0.0116 and −0.1034. Event-specific predecessor fits give respectively +0.0741, +0.0824 and +0.0024 for the first contrast, and +0.0371, +0.0354 and −0.1207 for the second. All 12 paired folio-bootstrap intervals include zero. In 32/32 synthetic trials with unchanged conditional log odds and shifted target and predecessor frequencies, both methods give a lower cross-line gain than either within-line comparison. The public trial establishes scan alignment in this sample but leaves Dominik’s prediction contrast unresolved.
check: Freeze a larger stratified sample of physical lines on new public leaves before obtaining image-based determinations. Have two separate readers first map row geometry then align the chosen loci and edge word groups; report gaps, intervening loci, uncertain separators and source-selection attrition. Verify the manuscript classes and the previous boundary model against the author’s full implementation if available. Compare the event-specific and transport models on matched triplets along with marginal-preserving common-association and reset controls. Report folio-level uncertainty and test whether endpoint imbalance or independent training refits can account for any measured gain gap.

source.title: Line-Conditioned Orthographic Organization in the Voynich Manuscript v1.0, Matthew Dominik, §3.3
source.note: The paper did not confirm any of its 30 scan candidates or release the full class/model definitions.

method.frame: Public practice folios, sampling before image retrieval by SHA-256 rank under K-042-open-2-v1. Select ten folios from six section/dialect strata with >=5 eligible transitions and then five pairs per folio. Every source witness had adjacent loci of unit P, sequential numbering, >=4 tokens per row and no paragraph end/start marker between.
method.visual: Three readers independently handled different assigned groups of unmarked 1800-pixel Yale images without transcripts or chosen-pair coordinates. Each saved row geometry before aligning selected loci with ZL edge groups. Ambiguous grouping was retained explicitly and excluded from the primary complete-case comparison.
method.training: Fit separately for ZL, IT, RF on public practice training leaves after excluding entire numbered leaves with a practice evaluation side. Classify by the first EVA character from acdefgiklmnopqrsy plus other. Require the two words in each compared pair to have no uncertainty character in all three witnesses for evaluation.
method.pairs: Compare upper last to lower first, lower first to second, and lower central adjacency from the same boundary triplet.
method.score: Natural log of predictive-probability ratio to a baseline for event, section/dialect and binned lower-row length. Each hierarchy level takes 24 pseudo-observations. The transferred model reweights the baseline by the pooled within-line predecessor probability divided by its marginal, and normalizes. The other fits separately by event within the training data with the same shrinkage mass. The bootstrap resamples folios, and the exploratory control permutes predecessor classes independently by folio and event. There are 4,999 draws of each.
method.controls: 32 independent seeds per regime. Equal conditional odds across events; equal odds with shifted class frequencies; true reset with the same shifted cross-line target marginal; and independence throughout. Oracle gains are enumerated for the binary population. Each simulation fits 2,110 triplets and tests 310.

limitations: The full classes, cut and fitted boundary model of the source were unspecified. The public estimate uses a declared alternative class encoding and models. The three witnesses cover the same physical rows; RF combines transcription sources. Each scan was read blind by one seat before its subsequent endpoint mapping, not independently by two. The main complete-case subset drops two sampled folios and cannot represent excluded uncertain alignments, foldouts beyond the selected panel, or the whole manuscript. Bootstrap results are conditional on trained models. Within-folio shuffling provides a descriptive comparison and does not guarantee exchangeability of physical lines.

a.method: Independent visual reading of five Yale jpgs only. Prose baselines follow top-to-bottom within a block. Horizontal fragment order is left-to-right. Each fragment is [x_left, y_left, x_right, y_right] in viewing images resized to width 900; multiply coordinates by two for the corresponding 1800-wide download. y is near the bottom of ordinary letter bodies, ignoring conspicuous ascenders and descenders. Values are approximate, generally within 5 viewing pixels, with greater uncertainty at the illustration and margins.

The repeated fragment slopes and row separations support the indicated left-to-right alignments. Row 3 of the upper block stretches toward the leaves and row 4 ends against the foliage. A small smudge over the top text lacks a prose baseline.

b.method: Image-only review. Scans reduced to 900 px width for visual row and coordinate reading, then coordinates doubled to the delivered 1800 px images. Baselines approximate; span ends trace row identity at text extremities and include no separate label where distinguishable. Row numbering is ordinal running-text row, separate from any transcription locus.

notes: Three unmistakable text blocks separated vertically by rows of illuminated roots and plants. Detached plant labels occur throughout the illustrations. Some run close to the last text line but I did not count them as prose.
First block slopes down to the right. Row 5 starts beside the upper jar and terminates appreciably left of row 4. The last strokes at its right fall just above illustrated greenery.

Middle block is partially constrained by roots at the left and leaf shapes at the right. Row 6 is slightly inset. Row 10 ends above a plant. Last block runs up against leaf/root contours to the right. Row 16 is short.
Large wide pool illustration between rows 19 and 20. The upper block is markedly sloped upward to the right through the first half; horizontal projection alone would mispair the edges.
The ornamental short ink stroke above upper-left row 1 is attached to an elevated glyph in that row. It is not a separately running line. The blue contour alongside the text is an illustration edge.
Rows 19 and 32 are noticeably short. Inside each main block no clearly interleaved detached text.

Continuous central field bounded by figures. Proposed visual runs use left-edge initials/short prior line; no large vertical gaps across the runs. The break between runs 4 and 5 is also an approximately 37 px leftward margin expansion at 900 px image width.

In parallel with row 15 at far right, a very short, detached inscription by the female figure at roughly (822,463) in 900 px view is excluded from running text. Check its association if the line endpoint matters.

A short detached inscription roughly (275,515) in 900 px view lies immediately to the left of row 17 alongside the figure, at nearly the same vertical position. I exclude it from prose provisionally based on its grouping with the figure and gap from the aligned left margin. It may be a same-baseline interleaving and needs separate alignment if an endpoint is sampled.
Several other detached labels sit above row 1 and beneath row 34 around figures and pipes. The central prose remains one physical column despite changing left and right boundaries.

c.method: Image-only visual count of running text in the original 1800 pixel wide Yale JPEGs using x strips and y rulers. y is approximate core-text baseline near each row start (allow about 8 pixels for endpoints), not the base of long descending strokes. Row ordinals are one-based in top-to-bottom visual reading order. Group indices describe observed layout.

reproduce.setup: From the project root with its verified data/raw directory, export the literal strings under files into a temporary directory, and export sample and physical_audit as sample.json and audit.json. Set PYTHONPATH to the project root.
reproduce.regenerate_sample: Download the pinned Yale manifest as manifest.json in the temporary directory and run python3 /path/to/temp/freeze.py /path/to/temp data/raw.
